pairs.evidence: crates/anon/Cargo.toml:6 The crate is a deterministic regex scrubber that depends only on regex and sha2 and runs no model against any scenario; a case-insensitive search of crates/anon for scenario, rubric, golden, candidate, trial and holdout found nothing, and its few 'judge' mentions are doc comments about a downstream reader.

pairs.subject: eval-harness
pairs.evidence: crates/store/src/conformance/mod.rs:58 The suite's only input is a Store backend and it asserts deterministic round-trips, which the golden path assigns to the test-harness subject; a case-insensitive search of crates/store/src for scenario, trial and holdout found nothing, and its judge and rubric strings are fixture data being round-tripped rather than a model being scored.

pairs.subject: eval-harness
pairs.evidence: crates/contract/src/endpoints/benchmarks.rs:21 The published contract makes a tier alias the default judge, and that alias resolves through a local roster table, so a roster revision changes the instrument behind every default-configured benchmark while its stored judge spec stays the same.

techniques.evidence: crates/contract/src/endpoints/benchmarks.rs:21 The technique says never an alias and names a tier constant as an alias with a local spelling; engine resolve_model maps opus to claude-opus-5, which is undated. The rest of the table is strong: labels.rs:117 keeps trust per rubric and scores.rs:101-102 refuses a regression across different instruments.
crates/contract/src/endpoints/scores.rs:100 The regression response gives case counts per failure family with a denominator, and a family that could not fire reads not_measured rather than zero.
crates/contract/src/endpoints/datasets.rs:175 Frozen sets are extended by forking to a new version rather than edited, so a finished run keeps the corpus it was scored against.
crates/contract/src/endpoints/scores.rs:60 Absolute, matrix and pairwise verdicts are separate kinds a reader can filter on, so one mode's numbers need not stand in for another's.

crates/contract/src/endpoints/benchmarks.rs:163 Covers this one write surface only: the scorecard door is machine-only with no MCP tool. Holdouts and the full read/write enumeration are not expressed in the table.
